qbm-definition-1-learning-problem: Definition 1 (Methods, p.3) defines the QBM learning problem; the value restates it.
qbm-classical-memory-assumption: Methods p.2: the authors state their classical-memory assumption (polynomial memory per sample, polynomially many samples) in place of access to copies of the target.
qbm-theorem-1-proof-ingredients: Checked against Supp. Note 3 (p.19-20): the proof does use the paper's own L-smoothness lemma, the SGD result of [27] (Lemma 8) and the shadow bound of [30]. This grades the authors' account of their method, not Theorem 1; two of the three ingredients are cited results.
qbm-hamiltonian-learning-not-solved: p.5: the authors state their result does not imply a solution to the stricter Hamiltonian learning problem with polynomially many samples. A caveat on scope.
qbm-theorem-3-pretraining: Theorem 3, p.5, proved in Supp. Note 4 (p.23-24) from the paper's own relative-entropy identity (Eq. 68); conditions (theta_0 = 0, other parameters fixed at zero) are in the statement. No cited theorem is used as a step.
qbm-maximally-mixed-not-most-distant: p.5: the authors' own caveat on the scope of Theorem 3, stated as a remark without proof.
qbm-lemma-7-l-smooth: Lemma 7, proved in Supp. Note 2 (p.17-18) from the paper's own Hessian bound and Gershgorin. The step ||Phi(V)|| <= ||V|| is argued tersely; quantum belief propagation (Lemma 5) is rederived in the paper (Eqs. 27-31).
qbm-relative-entropy-collinearity: Derived in full in the proof of Theorem 2 (Eq. 58, p.20-21), using only the stationarity condition (Eq. 32) and the existence of theta_opt.
qbm-expectation-error-bounds-relative-en: Eqs. (63) to (66), Supp. Note 3 (p.21-22): elementary derivation using the symmetrized relative entropy and the triangle inequality; no cited theorem.
qbm-single-qubit-parameter-sensitivity: Methods p.4: worked calculation for H = theta sigma_z, where <sigma_z> = tanh(theta); tanh(2.64) is 0.990 and tanh(3.8) is 0.999. The numbers check.
qbm-gibbs-prep-time-unknown: Introduction p.2: the caveat that polynomial sample complexity becomes irrelevant if Gibbs preparation is exponential is the authors' own limit. The 'exponential in the worst case' clause is cited to [32].
qbm-without-hidden-units-focus: Introduction p.1-2: the authors state they focus on QBMs without hidden units, and why.
qbm-numerical-targets-setup: Numerical experiments, p.6: XXZ Gibbs-state target and salamander retina data set, with 8-qubit problems for Fig. 2(a).
qbm-xxz-and-salamander-parameters: Supp. Note 5, p.27: J=-0.5, Delta=-0.7, h_z=-0.8, classical computation, first 8 features, first 10 recordings.
qbm-pretraining-models-defined: Mean-field (3n parameters) and Gaussian Fermionic (n^2 parameters) ansatzes are defined by the paper (p.6; Supp. Note 4), and the closed-form solutions are derived there.
qbm-pretraining-benefit-case-by-case: p.7 and Supp. Fig. 2: a caveat the authors state on their own simulations of pre-training, plus the scope note that Theorem 1 is proved only for a specific learning rate. True type: stated limit on a measured (simulation) result, not 'claim'.
qbm-constant-lr-no-guarantee: Supp. Note 3, p.22: the authors state no convergence guarantee exists for the constant learning rate they simulate. True type: stated limit on a measured (simulation) comparison, with a hedged ('may') instability caveat; not 'claim'.
qbm-numerical-single-run-limits: Supp. Note 3, p.22: few configurations and one SGD run each, for cost reasons. True type: stated limit on the measured (simulation) evidence, not 'setup'.
qbm-patent-competing-interest: Competing interests, p.9: the authors' own disclosure of affiliation and the pending patent application.
qbm-bounds-loose: Conclusions, p.8-9: the authors state their generic bounds are quite loose and a much smaller sample would do in practice. True type: stated limit on a theoretical bound, with the practical claim resting on their simulations (a measured result). The 'verified with classical numerical simulations' clause is in the same paragraph.
qbm-scope-no-hidden-units: The narrowed value is right: the Conclusions state the generality and the discussion of Theorem 1 (p.5) restricts the proved result to Pauli operators. The value attributes both to the authors, which is the authors' stated scope.
corli-review-scope-and-method: Section 1, p.2: the authors state the update date, the grouping by training method, and the preference for work with a practical implementation.
corli-review-selection-one-paper-per-cla: Section 1, p.3: 'we select and summarize a paramount paper for each of these classes'. The 'not exhaustive' reading follows directly.
gc-tree-parallel-decomposition-idea: Section 1.3, p.6: the authors' account of their method. Supported in the paper by Theorem 4.8, where the reflection through K costs one reflection through the circulation space plus O(1) gates, and by Definition 4.10 (tree-parallel decomposition).
gc-theorem-4-14-reflection-qrom: Theorem 4.14, p.24, proved on the page from Theorem 4.13 (proved in the paper) and QROM state preparation (Theorem 2.1, a standard tool).
gc-space-overhead-limit: Section 4.3, p.24 (and Section 1.3): the authors state the QROM space overhead is typically large and the classical precomputation may be exponential.
gc-qrom-weaker-than-qram: Section 2.2, p.9: the model assumption (read-only memory, unit-cost QROG) is defined in the paper; read-only being weaker than read-write follows from the definitions.
gc-computational-model-assumptions: Section 2.2, p.8: the success probability, the constant-time convention for elementary unitaries and the tilde convention are the paper's stated conventions.
gc-definition-span-program: Definitions 2.4 and 2.5, p.10, are the paper's own definitions.
gc-theorem-3-2-span-program-dual-adversa: Theorem 3.2, p.12, proved on the page by a direct calculation (a simplification of [Bel14, Theorem 3.39], but the proof is self-contained). The 1/sqrt(2) scaling is in the statement.
gc-theorem-3-3-two-subspace-to-transduce: Theorem 3.3, p.13, proved by checking the action on positive and negative instances. The comparison with earlier non-constructive transducer constructions is the author's remark.
gc-definition-graph-composition: Definition 4.5, p.17, is the paper's own definition.
gc-theorem-4-6-witness-sizes: Theorem 4.6, p.17-19, proved by chains of equivalences from Lemma 4.2 and Theorem 4.4, both proved in the paper.
gc-theorem-4-7-path-cut-bounds: Theorem 4.7, p.19, proved on the page from Theorem 4.6 by explicit unit flow and potential.
gc-theorem-5-2-st-to-graph-composition: Theorem 5.2, p.25, proved in a few lines from Theorem 4.6, with the conditions in the statement.
gc-theorem-5-4-planar-dual-negation: Theorem 5.4, p.26, proved from Lemma 5.3 (proved with Euler's formula, a textbook tool). The authors note it extends [JK17, Lemma 11], but the proof is in the paper.
gc-theorem-5-6-and-or-witness-sizes: Theorem 5.6, p.27: follows from Theorem 4.6 and the standard series and parallel resistance formulas.
gc-theorem-5-8-variable-time-formula-eva: Theorem 5.8, p.28, proved by induction on formula depth from Theorems 5.4, 5.6 and 4.14. The proof's final QROM bound O(d|J|) is tighter than the statement's O(|J|^(d+1)), so the statement is implied. The quotes thin out the statement.
gc-theorem-5-10-divide-and-conquer: Theorem 5.10, p.29, follows from Theorem 5.8 and Theorem 4.13 for Strategy 1 of [CKK+22] (Definition 5.9, taken as the definition). The Strategy 1 restriction is in the statement.
gc-theorem-5-17-wdt-to-st: Theorem 5.17, p.33, proved from Theorem 4.7 by explicit path and cut; the weighted-decision-tree complexity is defined in Definition 5.15.
gc-theorem-5-18-st-vs-wdt0: Theorem 5.18, p.34, proved by a parallel composition of the Theorem 5.17 programs weighted by the distribution.
gc-multidimensional-walk-limits: Section 5.5, p.35-36: the authors' own stated limits (technique not available in this framework; k-distinctness left for future work).
gc-lemma-5-23-gapped-majority: Lemma 5.23, p.38: the st bound is computed from Theorem 5.21's witness sizes (proved by induction in the paper); the R0 lower bound is a one-line argument that is correct.
gc-theorem-5-24-st-in-o-r: Theorem 5.24, p.38, proved by composing Lemma 5.23 with the decision-tree graphs of Theorem 5.17; the proof is terse but complete in the paper.
gc-lemma-6-10-dyck-depth-3-characterizat: Lemma 6.10, p.47-48, proved by a parity argument and case analysis on the prefix weight; the four conditions are in the statement.
gc-lemma-6-13-3-increasing-subsequence: Lemma 6.13, p.49-50, proved by contradiction on a minimal-extent subsequence.
randomized-algorithms-to-st-connectivity: Result 1.2 is Theorem 5.24 (p.38), proved from Lemma 5.23 and the Theorem 5.17 construction; the proof is terse but in the paper.
st-connectivity-subsumes-learning-graph-: The narrowed value is right: Theorem 5.13 (extended learning graph to st-connectivity, proof on p.31-32) and Theorem 5.18 (st at most sqrt(2) times WDT0, p.34) are proved in the paper, so the subsumption is up to a constant for the WDT framework.
st-vs-randomized-open-question: Open question 1.5, Section 1.2, p.5-6: the authors state what the paper leaves open.
correll-general-vrp-simplification: Section III, p.3: the authors state their model's simplifications of the Aisin problem.
correll-quantum-heads-cost-limit: Section IV B, p.6: the authors state the practical constraints (noise, access, monetary cost, queueing) on circuit count.
correll-model-configurations: Section V A, p.7: the two model configurations are as the value states (simulation-only: d=128, 8 heads, 16 qubits; hardware: d=64, 8 heads, 8 qubits, QONN for queries and keys in the encoder).
correll-training-emulated: Section V B, p.7-8: PyTorch state-vector emulation, efficient under about 30 qubits, with the authors' stated limit that stochastic and error behavior is not modeled.
correll-reinforce-baseline-setup: Section V C, p.8: the learning algorithm and baseline agent as the authors describe them.
correll-hardware-test-setup: Section VII A, p.10: 7 qubit counts times 10 parameter sets times 3 circuits is 210 circuits, 500 measurements each is 105,000. The numbers check.
correll-hardware-problem-simplified: Section VII B, p.11: the authors state the simplifications made for the hardware-sized problem and the reason.
correll-ionq-run-design: Section VII C, p.12-13: 8 nodes times 8 heads times 2 layers times 3 tomography steps is 384 circuits, 500 measurements each.
correll-limitations-few-approaches: Section VIII, p.13-14: the authors state they studied only a few approaches. The 'would likely find more efficient circuits' clause is their hedged outlook.
correll-cost-limit: Section VII C, p.13: the single IonQ run cost over USD 2000, and covering the whole supply chain this way would be enormously costly.
mild-problem-two-stage-deferral: Section 2, p.2-3: the paper defines the setting, deferral loss and common cost c_k = error + beta_k.
mild-expert-imbalance-definition: Appendix B, p.18: the paper's own definition of expert imbalance.
mild-lemmas-3-1-3-2-deferral-loss: Lemmas 3.1 and 3.2, p.3, proved in Appendix E (p.21) by elementary algebra; the cost normalization condition is stated. The proofs equate 1[f(x) != k] with 1[margin <= 0], exact except on score ties.
mild-cost-sensitive-margin-loss-definiti: Section 4.1, p.4: the paper defines the cost-sensitive margin loss and its imbalanced version.
mild-surrogate-and-algorithm-definition: Section 5.3, p.6: the paper defines MILD by its objective and surrogate.
mild-theorem-5-1-f-consistency: Theorem 5.1, p.6, proved in Appendix H (p.24-25) with the completeness condition stated; the proof uses Pinsker's inequality and Jensen (textbook tools).
mild-corollaries-5-2-5-3-deferral-bounds: Corollaries 5.2 and 5.3, p.7: follow from Theorem 5.1 by the reformulation shown in Section 5.3; the vanishing minimizability gap for F = Fall is the standard fact. Conditions are quoted.
mild-experiment-setup-image: Section 6, p.7-8: the image-experiment setup is as stated (five runs, four datasets, ResNet-18, Adam, batch 1,024, 200 epochs).
mild-expert-setups-and-costs: Section 6 and Appendix C.1, p.8 and p.18-19: coverage splits, synthetic and real experts, and the second cost (error plus coverage fraction) as stated.
mild-llm-routing-setup: Section 6.1 and Appendix C.2, p.8-9 and p.19: Qwen 2.5 experts, DeBERTa-v3-xsmall router, 5 epochs, 5e-5 AdamW, 4,000 training queries, 2,000 test samples, beta = [1.0, 0.6, 0.1].
mild-llm-optimal-expert-shares: Section 6.1, p.8 and Table 3: the optimal-oracle expert shares (82.2 percent; and 56.8 percent for Expert 3) under the two cost settings, as the authors report them for their benchmark subset.
mild-imbalance-is-over-experts: Section 1, p.2: the authors state the problem scope (imbalance over experts, not class labels). True type: scope (problem framing), not 'setup'. Wording: the passage says this 'complicates' direct use of imbalance techniques; the value's 'do not apply directly' is slightly stronger.

theory_low.qbm-theorem-1-training-sample-complexity: Supp. Note 3 proof of Theorem 1 uses Khaled and Richtarik [27], Corollary 1 (restated as Lemma 8), for the iteration count, and Huang et al. [30], Theorem 4, for the shadow-tomography sample count. Proof rests on two cited theorems.
theory_low.qbm-k-local-improved-shadow-bound: Eq. (11) is stated in the main text with no proof; it rests on cited shadow-tomography results [59], [43].
theory_low.qbm-no-barren-plateaus: The authors' consequence of Theorem 1 (p.5), itself graded low; no separate theorem or proof, and the 'no barren plateaus' reading is an interpretation.
theory_low.qbm-theorem-2-strongly-convex: Proof (Supp. Note 3) invokes Lemma 10, a restatement of Corollary 2 of Khaled and Richtarik [27], and Huang et al. [30] for the sample count. Also conditional on alpha-strong convexity, which the paper does not prove for general ansatzes.
theory_low.qbm-strong-convexity-unproven-general: Supp. Note 2, p.16: 'to the best of our knowledge' no proof exists in the literature; the second claim (proved for particular classes) is a cited result of Anshu et al. [53] and Haah et al. [54]. A statement about the literature, not a limit of the paper's own work.
theory_low.qbm-add-terms-without-retraining: A consequence the authors draw from Theorem 3 (p.5); not a theorem, and it holds only for pre-training that starts from the maximally mixed state, as the authors note.
theory_low.qbm-relative-entropy-strictly-convex: Lemma 6 (Supp. Note 2, p.15-16): convexity is shown from the Hessian, but strictness follows 'Proposition 17 in [53]' and uses Jaynes' principle [56] for existence. The paper's Definition 2 also defines strict convexity as a unique stationary point, which differs from the standard definition.
theory_low.qbm-jaynes-optimal-model-exists: The authors cite Jaynes' principle [56]; the existence claim is a cited result, not a setup choice of this paper.
theory_low.qbm-generalization-via-sampled-ansatz: Follows from the cited Theorem 4 (Theorem 1.1 of [64]) by the authors' argument; the authors state it is not tested numerically.
theory_low.qbm-conclusion-polynomial-gibbs-preparat: Restates Theorem 1, whose proof rests on cited SGD [27] and shadow-tomography [30] results.
theory_low.qbm-mean-field-closed-form: Eqs. (70) to (77) derive the closed form directly, but the claim of existence and uniqueness 'provided the target set is consistent' rests on strict convexity (Lemma 6, graded low) and fails at the boundary: a pure-state target (norm of the expectation vector equal to 1) gives infinite parameters.
theory_low.qbm-gaussian-fermionic-closed-form: Supp. Note 4, p.25-26: Eq. (80) is asserted, not derived, and uniqueness is argued from 'the eigendecomposition of a Hermitian matrix is unique', which is false for degenerate eigenvalues. Not a proof.
theory_low.qbm-poly-gibbs-states: The narrowed value is right (fully-visible QBM, sample complexity only), but the 'proves' claim is Theorem 1, whose proof rests on cited results [27] Corollary 1 and [30] Theorem 4.; team lead, 2026-11-04, Sprint 15 Manual Validation Q1 option 1 (all 36 as proposed)
theory_low.qbm-pretraining-lowers-bound: Theorem 3 itself is proved in the paper (see qbm-theorem-3-pretraining). 'Lowers the sample complexity bounds' needs the delta_0 dependence of Theorem 1's iteration count, which rests on cited results; so the whole claim grades by the weaker part.; team lead, 2026-11-04, Sprint 15 Manual Validation Q1 option 1 (all 36 as proposed)
theory_low.gc-result-1-3-divide-conquer-subspace-gr: Informal Result 1.3. Footnote 1 restricts divide-and-conquer to Strategy 1 of [CKK+22], which the quotes drop. Theorem 5.20's witness analysis is taken from [JP24, Section 3.3], a cited analysis.
theory_low.gc-result-1-4-gt-d-bounds: Informal Result 1.4. Theorem 5.25 uses [CMP22, Theorem 5.4] and [CMP22, Corollary 1.7]; Theorem 5.28's tightness proof uses [EH89, Lemma 1] and [FG06, Lemma 16.19].
theory_low.gc-st-vs-q-separation-unknown: The first claim is the authors' stated limit, but 'equal for the usual suspects' (OR, majority, parity, tribes, indexing) is asserted without proof or citation in Section 5.7, so the value is weaker than a stated limit.
theory_low.gc-st-vs-r-quadratic-separation: Section 5.7, p.41: a field statement about known separations; the quote is cut where the text layer drops the square root, and R(OR) in Omega(n) is a known result not proved here.
theory_low.gc-theorem-3-5-span-program-algorithm-co: Proof (p.13-14) says the cost claims are 'readily verified' and takes the error analysis from [BY23, Section 7.4], a cited result.
theory_low.gc-lemmas-4-11-4-12-decomposition: The quotes carry only the two lemma titles, not the statements. The proofs are in the paper (p.21-22) and appear sound, so a re-quote of the statements would support HIGH, proved result.
theory_low.gc-every-graph-has-tree-parallel-decompo: Section 4.3, p.21: an informal inductive remark ('we remark that...'), not a proved statement; the depth bound |E| is asserted in the same remark.
theory_low.gc-theorem-5-7-variable-time-search: Proved on p.27-28 from Theorem 5.6, but the statement's formula is garbled in the text layer and the quotes carry only the lead-in sentence and title, so the conditions are not carried.
theory_low.gc-theorem-5-11-directed-st-connectivity: Statement's exponent is broken in the text layer, and the value's closing simplification ('square root of two to the log n') is not what the paper's O(2^(log^2 n / 2) polylog n) bound reduces to. The improvement is over [JP24, Theorem 5.3].
theory_low.gc-theorem-5-19-5-20-phase-estimation-su: Theorem 5.19 is proved on the page, but Theorem 5.20 builds on the subspace-graph definitions of [JP24] and says 'the witness analysis follows directly from [JP24, Section 3.3]', a cited analysis. The value holds both.
theory_low.gc-theorem-5-21-threshold-optimal: Optimality is cited to [Bel14, Proposition 3.32]. The text-layer statement C = k(n+k-1) disagrees with the paper's own witness sizes (W+ W- = k(n-k+1)), so the value repeats an inconsistent complexity.
theory_low.gc-theorem-5-22-exact-weight-optimal: Optimality rests on [Rei09, Proposition A.7], a cited result. The witness-size computation is in the paper, but the statement is built on Theorem 5.21's inconsistent scaling constant.
theory_low.gc-theorem-5-25-d-at-most-wdt-squared: Proof uses [CMP22, Theorem 5.4] (recursion for WDT of a tree) and modifies the proof of [CMP22, Corollary 1.7]. Corollary 5.26 follows from it.
theory_low.gc-theorem-5-27-gt-vs-wdt: Proof is 'analogous to Theorem 5.25' (which rests on [CMP22]) and is brief.
theory_low.gc-theorem-5-28-tight-separation: The tightness proof uses [EH89, Lemma 1] and [FG06, Lemma 16.19], cited results; the statement is broken in the text layer and the quotes do not carry its conditions.
theory_low.gc-graph-composition-query-optimal: Section 5.7, p.39: an informal argument that relies on the completeness of span programs and the dual adversary bound, cited results, not proved here.
theory_low.gc-fig1-2-relations-read: A diagram of relations read from Figure 1.2; the individual relations are graded under their own theorems, and several of those are LOW.
theory_low.gc-theorem-6-2-aperiodic-pattern-matchin: The proof uses Lemma 6.1 (deterministic sample), taken from Vishkin [Vis91], as the key step for the negative witness. Time and QROM bounds are also argued briefly.
theory_low.gc-theorem-6-3-periodic-pattern-matching: The proof uses Lemma 6.1 [Vis91] for the period's deterministic sample; the time bound is left for future work, as the value says.
theory_low.gc-theorem-6-5-or-psearch-tight: Tightness rests on the lower bound of [AKV23, Theorem 2], a cited result, and the time and QROM bounds are only sketched (a halving decomposition). The query upper bound is proved.
theory_low.gc-theorem-6-7-dynamic-and-or: The query bound is proved (Section 6.2.2), but the time bound is argued by reference to the Theorem 6.5 sketch (and says O(sqrt n) levels, which is an apparent slip for O(log n)); recovering [CKK+22, Theorem 4] is a comparison.
theory_low.gc-theorem-6-9-dyck-depth-1-2: The statement is cut in the text layer, so the quotes do not carry its conditions; the proof is a few lines and calls the lower bound 'a simple reduction to search'.
theory_low.gc-theorem-6-11-dyck-depth-3: The query bound is proved from Lemma 6.10, but the time bound is argued by reference to Theorems 6.5 and 6.7 ('the same divide and conquer strategy'), which is a sketch.
theory_low.gc-theorem-6-14-3-increasing-subsequence: The query bound is proved from Lemma 6.13, but the time bound is argued by reference to Theorems 6.5, 6.7 and 6.11, which is a sketch.
theory_low.wdt-speedup-at-most-quadratic: The narrowed value is right (the barrier applies to the WDT and GT frameworks, not st-connectivity), but it follows from D at most WDT^2 (Theorem 5.25, which rests on [CMP22]) and Theorems 5.27 and 5.28, graded low, and it is stated as an interpretation.; team lead, 2026-11-04, Sprint 15 Manual Validation Q1 option 1 (all 36 as proposed)
theory_low.mild-deferral-as-cost-sensitive-input-ex: The equality E[Ldef] = E[l_def] holds only up to an additive constant (Lemmas 3.1/3.2). 'Probability inversely proportional to cost' is loose: the rewards are 1-c_k or the sum of other costs, which decrease in c_k but are not inversely proportional.
theory_low.mild-theorem-4-1-margin-bound: Proof (Appendix F) uses the vector contraction lemma (Maurer 2016; Cortes et al. 2016c) as a key step, a cited result; the inequalities are also broken in the text layer.
theory_low.mild-margin-tradeoff: An interpretation of the bound in the discussion after Theorem 4.1, not a theorem.
theory_low.mild-corollary-4-2-explicit-bound: Rests on Theorem 4.1 (low) and on the Rademacher-complexity bound of Eq. (3), which is stated without proof; the bound is broken in the text layer.
theory_low.mild-optimal-rho-claim: 'It is straightforward to show': no derivation in the paper; the formula is broken in the text layer.

requote.mild-imbalance-is-over-experts: the stored value said standard techniques 'do not apply directly'; the paper says the distinction 'complicates' their direct application

value_replace.mild-imbalance-is-over-experts: The authors state that the imbalance they address concerns experts, not class labels, and that this distinction complicates the direct application of traditional imbalance-handling techniques.
